subject: Clarify: SOC2 interim-gap vs overlap treatment for Type II coverage
messages:
From: BrightLayer Audit <audits@brightlayer.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Legal <legal@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Questions on SOC2 Type II coverage window (interim gap vs overlap)

Hi Rafael,

Thanks again for sending the initial evidence manifest. While preparing fieldwork we noticed Acme's Type II report period is listed as 2026-04-01 through 2026-06-30, but there are two operational events we want to confirm how you prefer to represent in the report/bridge: an in-place migration that created an overlapping snapshot window on 2026-05-01 (some services duplicated across environments for ~36 hours) and an interim maintenance outage on 2026-05-18 02:00–05:30 UTC.

Two specific asks:
1) For the overlap around 2026-05-01, do you treat the overlap as inclusive (both environments considered in-scope for May) or do you treat it as a point-in-time snapshot where only the active environment at a given timestamp is counted? Our auditors prefer explicit language either way to avoid ambiguity in control testing.
2) For the 2026-05-18 outage, would you prefer we document it as an exception inside the Type II period, or request a bridge letter that explicitly covers the outage window and any revised sampling approach?

Attached is the evidence_manifest.csv (sample). Can you confirm preferred wording and whether you can provide a draft bridge letter (or approval for us to prepare one for your review)? Also let us know the timestamp format we should expect for the log extracts (UTC with millisecond precision is preferred).

Thanks,

Lena Park
Senior Auditor
BrightLayer Audit

Attachment: evidence_manifest.csv (CSV listing evidence files and collection windows)

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>
To: BrightLayer Audit <audits@brightlayer.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Acme Legal <legal@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on SOC2 Type II coverage window (interim gap vs overlap)

Lena — thanks for the clear write-up. Looping in Olga (Head of Security Ops) to confirm operational intent and to draft a short bridge letter if needed. Quick answers up-front:

- Overlap on 2026-05-01: our policy for migrations is to treat control evidence by point-in-time behavior. In practice we map each control evidence item to the environment that produced the primary authoritative artifact at the recorded timestamp. That said, for legal/audit clarity we're fine with a statement that explains the temporary duplication and that control testing used timestamped artifacts to assign events to the correct environment.

- Outage on 2026-05-18: we would prefer a short bridge letter that documents the outage window and the compensating controls used (enhanced monitoring and post-incident change review). If BrightLayer prefers to draft and send us a proposed language we can review and sign.

For logs: we can provide UTC timestamps with millisecond precision (ISO 8601) and an example sample (attached).

I'll attach a very short proposed bridge draft for your convenience. Olga — can you confirm the language around the duplication/point-in-time assignment and whether we should list both environments explicitly in the bridge or keep it more descriptive?

Best,
Rafael
Head of Sales (Enterprise)
Redwood Inference

Attachments: proposed_bridge_draft.docx, timestamped-log-sample.txt

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, BrightLayer Audit <audits@brightlayer.com>
Cc: Acme Legal <legal@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 12:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on SOC2 Type II coverage window (interim gap vs overlap)

Thanks — quick clarifying points from security operations: 

1) For the 2026-05-01 migration duplication: do not list internal environment hostnames in the bridge. Instead, we propose a paragraph that states there was a short period of dual-running during a controlled migration and that control evidence was attributed by timestamp to the environment generating the evidence. Suggested sentence: "A controlled migration resulted in temporary dual-running of certain services on 1 May 2026; evidence was attributed to the environment that produced the authoritative log entry at the recorded timestamp."

2) For the 18 May outage: we will provide a single signed bridge letter that:
   - states the exact outage window in UTC,
   - summarizes compensating controls (real-time monitoring, incident review), and
   - references the log extracts and post-incident change tickets included in the evidence bundle.

I can redline Rafael's draft and return it by EOD PST. If BrightLayer wants to provide a proposed wording that would speed things up.

—Olga
Director, Security Operations
Redwood Inference

From: BrightLayer Audit <audits@brightlayer.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael_mendes@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Legal <legal@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Aug 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Questions on SOC2 Type II coverage window (interim gap vs overlap)

Thanks Rafael and Olga — that proposed approach sounds reasonable and audit-friendly. A couple of remaining items before we schedule evidence testing: 

- Please push the redlined bridge letter and we will review. If you prefer, we can send a short template and you can sign.
- For the log extracts, please include a brief manifest (CSV) with: file name, start_timestamp_utc, end_timestamp_utc, timezone (UTC), and the system name (high-level label only). Millisecond precision is fine.
- For our report wording we'll prefer: "temporary dual-running during a controlled migration; evidence was attributed to the environment that produced the authoritative log entry at the recorded timestamp." If you can confirm you'll accept that exact sentence (or close variant) we'll use it.

Once we have the signed bridge and manifest we'll schedule sampling and control testing.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Lena Park
Senior Auditor
BrightLayer Audit

Attachment: audit-template-bridge.docx (we'll upload after internal check)
